shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling/needs/work/storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a 146,000-cell budget; colder with altitude, richer ore and more cave with depth. Coast, river and lake tiles supported; Dubs Mint Minimap and Map Preview both patched. Rendering, interaction and generation all verified in play.
body:
# As above, So below II — V2

> V1 is **DELETED**. ~65 files / ~17,000 LOC.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

> **Visuality pass (runs #167-171) COMPLETE — all seven reported items closed and verified in play.**
> **QOL pass (five items) WRITTEN, BUILD GREEN, UNTESTED IN PLAY** — see §15.

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount × Slot)`; bands along **+z** from the deepest basement; permanently-fogged gutter between bands; `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)×64` — **64-alignment is load-bearing**. Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254, each just under a 64 boundary.

### The one insight
`Region.Neighbors` is **topological, not spatial**. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms/temperature/vacuum; `Reachability.CanReach` works **unpatched**. **But reachability ≠ a path** — 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

### Hard 1.6 constraints
Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell ⇒ **total stacked cells is the runtime metric** · no `PathFinder.FindPath` · `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE — the recurring shape of every generation bug
The surface band is a horizontal SLICE of a tall map, so **anything vanilla anchors to the map's extent lands in the wrong band**. Four instances, each with a different fix shape:
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Anchor** — a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river / lake centre (§6b); random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| **Field** — a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| **Noise space** — a slice ≠ a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| **Distance-to-extent** — a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b/§15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
**Classify a new generation bug into one of these four before theorising.** Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN — cell budget = **146,000**
`4 × 190 = 145,920` sets the figure; `2 × 254 = 130,048`, `7 × 126 = 112,896`; `5 × 190` and `7 × 190` refused (3-up-and-3-down at 190 auto-drops to 126 — the intended trade).
`ABMapSizeLimit` owns it: `UpperLevels`/`LowerLevels` (0-3), `BandCount`, `SurfaceBand = lower`, `Fits`, `MaxSize`, `MaxLevelsFor`, `StackedCells`. `ABV2.BandCount`/`SurfaceBand` are properties (were consts — the only thing pinning the mod to 3 levels).
**Per-level size is SQUARE (`Size.x == bandHeight`)** — this is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (which squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count and needs no scaling. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.

### ⚠ THE CHOOSER UI — own the widget, don't patch the data
**`Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play.** Vanilla's group headers only render for 200/250/300, so their presence in a screenshot proved our array was never used. The postfix also re-snapped `GameInitData.mapSize` **every frame**, undoing every click.
**Now:** our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly; vanilla sizes locked; strip shows cells-used-vs-budget. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix — **vanilla lays its columns from the top and never consults the height, so added space is ours.**

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix → tick sweep → `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` **BFSes the band graph**; hops must strictly decrease or pawns ping-pong.
**Caveat:** an intermediate level must be walkable between arrival and the next staircase. **STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING — three wrong layers before the right one
`GetOptions` clickPos (wrong layer) → per-pawn `BestOrderedGotoDestNear` (fought vanilla's formation) → **correct:** `RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 don't") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix = normalise `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. **Verified.**

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE — `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated `drop`. **NINE systems share it**, including both shadow layers and `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen`.
**SEVEN appearances of the single-`- Slot` bug.** #6/#7 were the shadow layers — from +1 the step lands on the opaque surface and works; from +2/+3 it lands in OPEN AIR, which holds no edifices. **VERIFIED FIXED (#168): shadows correct on every upper level.**
**Sun-shadow subtlety:** its mask is *neighbour*-based (a mountain-edge caster sits under an opaque cap and can never resolve a descent of its own), so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the **smallest** drop among the nine cells.
**Still single-band:** the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION — verified in play
**⚠ FOUR REJECTED ATTEMPTS:** force-linked wall masks · high-queue cover · wall-sprite suppression · theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (**wall dissolves only at 7+ open neighbours** — at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge) · one central fog hole · five-terrain plateau palette · cliff faces · alpine pass (shallow-only tarns, per-cell 6-cell edge rule, rim scree, exposure-thinned flora).
**Cross-band decoration:** `EmitMassSilhouetteAt`/`EmitMeadowFadeAt` emit into ANY layer at a z offset.
**Ore glyph bug:** ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` ⇒ a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole **atlas sheet** per cell.

# 6b. ⚠ WATER — `ABWaterV2.cs`. **1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect**
`SectionLayer_Watergen` renders `waterDepthMaterial` into the **WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's** texture; the visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that (`_WaterOutputTex`) **at its own screen position**. Printing the water material where the depth pass never wrote yields **nothing at all**.
- **Water vanished from upper levels — VERIFIED FIXED (#171).** Half a two-pass effect was missing. `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` mirrors vanilla's `internal` Watergen (`waterDepthMaterial` + water-to-water edge fans for shorelines), descends via `TryResolveVisibleBelow`, **overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`**. Proven by the bisect toggle.
- **Rivers "did not generate" — VERIFIED FIXED (#167).** `GetRiverCenter` picks `Rand.Range(0.3f,0.7f) × map.Size.z`. Remapped into the surface band preserving the *roll*. Patched on `GetRiverCenter`, **not** `Init`. **`GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.** Proof: `band 0 baseRiver=3079`, all others `0`.
- **Water ran north-south even in lakes — RESOLVED**, most likely as a side effect of the river fix. Not independently proven.
- **⚠ REJECTED — DO NOT RETRY: republishing `_MapSize` as one band.** Fitted every symptom; **DISPROVED IN ONE LAUNCH** — banding the global is what MAKES water run north-south.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP — active level only. **VERIFIED (#169)**
Reflection-only, **no foreign type in any signature**. Detection by **type presence**, not packageId.
**ONE RECT, NOT SEVEN PATCHES.** Their six draw passes all take the same `radarRect` and are LINEAR in position: `height = view.height*Size.z/H`, `y = view.height*(H + bandMin - Size.z)/H`. **Culling is free.**
**Their texture blit cannot be reused:** `DrawTextureFitted` fits **preserving the TEXTURE's aspect**. Drawn with `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. `CameraDriver.CurrentRealPosition` is **private** (Dubs publicises Assembly-CSharp); `Find.Camera.transform.position` is the same value.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW — surface band only. `MapPreviewCompat.cs`. **VERIFIED (#171)**
Map Preview never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap`, so our banding prefix never fires — and the surface band is a SLICE, so **position-based noise makes it a different map, not a slightly wrong one**.
**Fix = generate at full stacked height, show only the band's rows.** Most of it is NOT Harmony: `MaxMapSize`/`MapSizeOverride` are public static fields (their own `ModCompat_BetterMapSizes` is the precedent). `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500; a stack reaches 896). Three patches: postfix `DetermineMapSize` (the CLAMPED entry point) gated to player-colony parents; postfix `MapPreviewResult.get_TexCoords` to crop; postfix `OnWorldTileSelected` to restate window width.
**`TryPendingSurfaceRect` falls back to a SIZE-INFERRED layout** so every generation-time patch behaves identically during a preview — including §15's `CloseToEdge`. Safe because `bandCount * Slot` always exceeds the width once more than one band exists.

# 6e. ⚠ COASTLINES — coastal tiles are multi-level. **VERIFIED (#171)**
Symptom (#170): a coastal colony with its **entire surface band underwater** — `36100 water` out of exactly 36100 cells. **100%, and that precision was the diagnosis.**
**THE FALLOFF IS NOT SCALED WRONG, IT IS CENTRED WRONG.** `map.Size.z` appears in `FalloffAtAngle` in exactly ONE place: the final `Translate(-x/2, 0, -z/2)`. The coast gradient is **already one band wide** and merely sits at the middle of the whole STACK.
**Fix:** `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`. **NO SCALING, deliberately.**
**ONE PATCH COVERS THE FAMILY:** nine coastal mutators derive from `TileMutatorWorker_Coast` and **none override `GetNoiseValue`**.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Sky temp `-4°C × level` (compounds) · basement flat -6 · ore `×(1+0.45×(depth-1))`, cave openness `×(1+0.35×(depth-1))`, both AFTER the settings clamp · mountains taper upward for free.
**Snow line:** generation-time seeding **REMOVED**. Vanilla melts/accumulates per-CELL temperature and the per-level offset already makes high levels cold — earned, not painted on at t=0.

# 8. CAMERA
`freeCameraPan` REMOVED. `ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by **level**; **`maxZoom` left DERIVED** (an absolute would mis-scale a 190 band). **`panMargin` 63.5 now applies to EVERY level** (§15c). `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED — **a calibration tool must suspend the limit it calibrates.** Clamp bails while `Scribe` is active or state isn't `Playing`.

# 9. ⚠ GENERATION COST — the top open item
| Config | Tile | Cells | Carve | Things destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 × 190 | — | 109,440 | 5.0 s | 14,971 |
| 7 × 126 | — | 112,896 | 30.4 s | 62,686 |
| 4 × 190 (#167) | **river** | 145,920 | 18.7 s | 56,318 |
| 4 × 190 (#168) | sparse | 145,920 | 2.5 s | 15,787 |
| 4 × 190 (#169) | sparse+road | 145,920 | 2.1 s | 13,913 |
| 4 × 190 (#171) | **coast** | 145,920 | 15.2 s | 50,585 |
**`Sky clear` is ~97% of the carve**; **`0 rocks spawned`**.
**⚠ THE REAL DRIVER IS BIOME CONTENT, NOT CELL COUNT** — 9× spread at identical size. **Any carve timing MUST record the tile or it is meaningless.**
**THE FIX — extend the doomed-band genstep skip** (precedent: `Patch_WildPlantSpawner_ABSkipDoomedBands`, 16.9 s → 4.2 s). Targets: `RocksFromGrid`, `Terrain`, `RockChunks`, `Plants`, `ScatterRuinsSimple`, `CaveHives`.
**HARD CONSTRAINT: per-cell gensteps scope safely; `map.Area`-count scatterers do NOT** (but see §2 — the scatterer family counts off `Size.x²`, so it is safe). **Do not blanket-skip the water/coast mutators.**

# 10. RUNTIME PERF — 59.6 fps @96 pawns, mod ≈2% frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry.

# 11. VERTICAL LINKS — elevator SHIPPED, **untested**. Full-mesh 2×2; O(n²) in band count.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
band info · **below layer report** · below pawn report · **water report** · transit health · stuck probe · transit logging · lighting/shader/biome reports · bisect toggles (incl. **below water depth**) · ABGenProfile · camera calibration.
**The start-spot failure log is a first-class diagnostic** — its cell census identified the coastline bug in one line.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Play-test the QOL pass (§15)** — five items, all untested.
2. **Doomed-band genstep scoping pass** (§9) — band 1 first, and record the tile.
3. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators** — Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
4. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix, lake-anchor patch.
5. Realtime-things pass still single-band (motes/fire >1 level down).
6. Selection bracket **drifts upward as you zoom out**.
7. **Option E — waterfalls**: de-risked by §6b.
8. COMBAT never verified · Option C parked · vertical conduit · compat audit incl. Better Mountains · transplant · **store page still says three levels**.

# 14. LESSONS (telegraphic)
**Run the diagnostic before the third theory** · **build the A/B discriminator INTO any change whose mechanism you cannot read** · **a beautiful fit is not evidence** · **an EXACT number is a diagnosis** · **the ABSENCE of a known error line is a valid pass signal** · **poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts** · **when N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter instead of patching N sites** · **find the ONE virtual everything funnels through** — nine coastal mutators / every scatterer's `CanScatterAt` / one `CloseToEdge` · **read the foreign mod's OWN compat classes first** · **check which OVERLOAD a foreign call binds to** · **never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature** · **re-centre, don't rescale** · **anything anchored to the map's extent lands in the wrong band; classify it as anchor / field / noise-space / distance-to-extent** · **position-based noise means a SLICE of a tall map ≠ a short map** · **an odd/even or count-dependent symptom is arithmetic** · **a UNIFORM symptom is a scale/constant, a PATCHY one is data** · **when a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes** · measure, don't extrapolate · **two runs of the same config are only comparable if the TILE matches** · **a single-step assumption survives until the data has two steps — grep every `- Slot`** · **patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it** · **own the widget instead of patching the data it reads** · **ALTITUDE IS DRAW ORDER — check where a new overlay sorts against `WorldClipper` before blaming the thing it hides** · **`Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation** — generation-time patches must read the pending layout · never hide sprites that carry gameplay information · ore defs have no naturalTerrain · a `Graphic_Linked` base material is the whole ATLAS SHEET · **"can't happen" fallbacks are what the player photographs** · enforce spatial rules PER CELL · **balance GUI clip/group pops in a `finally`** · statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak — CWT, or store the id only as a change DETECTOR · **Unity textures are not GC'd with their owner** · **any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`** · never cache comps while Scribe active · FinalizeInit = worker thread · `SectionLayer` subclasses are **auto-discovered**.

---

# 15. QOL PASS — five items. **BUILD GREEN, NONE TESTED IN PLAY**

## 15a. Nothing may exist in the void — `ABBandSafety.cs`
Pawns were spawning in the GUTTER, where there is no region: they cannot path, cannot be reached, and cannot be rescued by any ordinary mechanism.
**Three layers, deliberately redundant:**
- **The finders** — `CellFinder.RandomEdgeCell(Rot4,Map)`, the 5-arg `TryFindRandomEdgeCellWith`, and `CellFinder.RandomCell` now answer inside the SURFACE band. (The two no-dir overloads were already redirected in `ABBandEnv`; `RCellFinder.TryFindRandomPawnEntryCell` funnels through one of those and was already covered.)
- **The choke point** — a prefix on the 7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn` (every overload funnels into it) rewrites `loc` before vanilla reads it, so nothing downstream ever observes the bad cell. **Scoped to Pawns and to the GUTTER only** — a pawn spawning on a non-surface band is legitimate and must not be dragged anywhere.
- **The sweep** — `[ABGameTick]` every 120 ticks, `Position` + `Notify_Teleported` (the vanilla teleport idiom; the Position setter does the thingGrid bookkeeping). Catches teleports, psycasts, foreign spawners and pre-fix saves.
**Relocation is ALWAYS to the surface**, by decision: a spawn that landed in the void has already proven its chooser does not understand bands, so the nearest band is an accident of which seam it fell into, not evidence of intent.
Inert during generation (`Banded` is false there) — that window has `RescueStrandedColonists`, which knows what the carve is about to delete.

## 15b. Structures must not straddle a seam — `CloseToEdge`, re-based
**Root cause is the slicing rule's fourth shape.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measures against `map.Size`, so on a stack z==0 is the deepest basement's floor and z==Size.z-1 is the top of the sky: **the surface band reports itself as inland everywhere, including the two rows that butt onto a seam.** Every generator's "keep away from the edge" declaration was therefore silently void.
**One prefix re-bases the distance onto the cell's OWN band rect** (live via `ABBands`, mid-generation via `TryPendingSurfaceRect`). Eleven call sites in the whole game, all cold — and they all inherit the fix using their own declared numbers: `GenStep_Scatterer`'s `minEdgeDist`/`extraNoBuildEdgeDist`/`minEdgeDistPct`, `DropCellFinder.distToEdge`, ruin edifice trimming, the zone-edge rule.
**Backstop:** a postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt` rejects cells within 10 of a band's Z seam, for gensteps that declare no margin at all. Z only — a band's X edges ARE the map's X edges. Skipped when the band is too short to afford it. Postfixing the base reaches the whole family because every stock override opens with `if (!base.CanScatterAt(...)) return false;`.

## 15c. Camera bounds — one row for every level
`ABCameraBounds.For` gave the measured `panMargin` 63.5 to levels +1..+3 and a hard 0 to the surface and below, purely because calibration had only ever been run in the sky. In play the ground floor — where nearly all play happens — was the one level whose framing felt broken. **There was never a per-level reason:** `panMargin` is a framing choice only, and `Patch_CameraDriver_ABClipViewToBand` guarantees overhang shows curtain and never the neighbouring level, on any level. Now uniform; the `switch` is kept as the place a genuinely per-level value would go.

## 15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge — REMOVED on banded maps. `ABNoBuildEdge.cs`
Both halves were anchored to the stack: **functionally** the 10-cell strip landed on the deepest basement's floor and the top of the sky and nowhere else; **visually** `GenDraw.DrawMapEdgeLines` boxes `Find.CurrentMap.Size`, so the dashed rectangle framed the whole 190×768 stack and was usually off-screen entirely.
Removed rather than re-based — **per-band is one flag away** (`ABNoBuildEdge.Removed`), because 15b already re-bases the underlying test, so simply dropping the two overrides yields a correct per-level strip. Removed because a level's north/south boundary is the seam: an internal structural device the player did not choose and should not build around, and ten cells of every level is real space on a 126 band.
**Stated consequence:** vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its own map edge and starving the pawn-entry finder.
The no-**zone** edge rule is KEPT (and is now per-band for free via 15b); only its stray whole-stack overlay box is suppressed, since `DrawMapEdgeLines` is private and takes only a distance.

## 15e. Drop pods fall through the levels — `ABSkyfallerRelay.cs`
**Two faults, one symptom** ("pods pop in just above the ground; a pod bound for another level is never seen"):
1. **The curtain ate the flight.** A skyfaller's `DrawPos` is its landing cell plus an animation offset starting tens of cells north, so for most of the descent it is drawn OUTSIDE its own band — and `AltitudeLayer.WorldClipper` (the curtain) sorts **above** `AltitudeLayer.Skyfaller`. Nothing was broken; it was being painted over.
2. **A pod bound elsewhere was culled** by the band-clipped view rect — but a descending pod physically passes through every level above its target.
**One mechanism for both:** suppress vanilla's per-thing draw (prefix on `Skyfaller.DrawAt` — reached only by skyfallers, unlike `Thing.DynamicDrawPhaseAt` which every dynamic thing walks every frame) and re-issue it once via `DrawNowAt`, translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Suppressing the whole body parks the drop-spot shadow too, which is correct: the relay's call re-runs the same body, so the shadow draws exactly once at the real landing cell, at its own low altitude — visible when its level is on screen, behind the curtain when it is not.
**Altitude is chosen PER FRAME:** normal while the pod is over its own level (so lighting, weather and fog still sit on it), lifted above `WorldClipper` only while it is out over the curtain. Lifting unconditionally would render every landing at full brightness through the night lighting overlay — a worse bug, visible only after dark.
**Pass-through timing:** shown for all but the last `levelsAbove × 18` ticks so it sinks out of the level instead of appearing to land on our floor; outgoing (`reversed`) skyfallers get the mirror rule off `ageTicks`. `levelsAbove == 0` reduces exactly to vanilla.
Registry is a `ConditionalWeakTable` keyed by the Map OBJECT, pruned lazily on the draw pass (one liveness test covers Destroy / DeSpawn / impact / map removal). `Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` is excluded — it OVERRIDES `DrawAt`, so the suppression never fires for it and relaying would double-draw.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`. Companions: drop them when a bug might not be ours. **Compat tests need the target mod as a companion** — Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`) and Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`) are both INACTIVE in the user's real list. Multi-level tests need `quicktest=false`; **Map Preview doubly so**. **Water tests need a river or lake tile; coastline tests a coastal one** — note the tile in any perf comparison. **A `surfaceBand=0` config cannot exercise band-folded addressing** — use lower levels for that.
**QOL pass specifically:** needs a colony with levels ABOVE the surface (so a pod can be watched from a level above its target), a raid or trader caravan (edge spawns), and a build designator dragged to a level's north/south edge.
